rules.title: Ban on sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms for rents and occupancy (Ord. 7,992-N.S. amending BMC ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell or provide, coordinated pricing algorithms that use non-public competitor data to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. The city attorney or an aggrieved tenant can sue for up to $1,000 per violation, and each unit and each month is a separate violation.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores no pueden usar, ni los proveedores vender u ofrecer, algoritmos coordinados de precios que utilicen datos no públicos de competidores para fijar o recomendar alquileres o niveles de ocupación en viviendas residenciales de Berkeley. La Fiscalía Municipal o un inquilino afectado pueden demandar por hasta $1,000 por infracción, y cada unidad y cada mes cuenta como una infracción separada.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley and their landlords; sellers/licensors of coordinated pricing algorithms to Berkeley landlords.
rules.exemptions: Excludes aggregated, anonymous rental data reports that do not recommend rents; products used to set affordable housing rent or income limits; market research for project financing, appraisals, and research, testing or training for software development.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.penalty: Civil action by City Attorney or aggrieved tenant for damages, injunctive relief, restitution, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees to the prevailing party.
rules.caveat: The document shows the ordinance only as 'passed to print' at the November 18, 2025 meeting; final adoption and effective date are not shown in the document.
